page: Microsoft Azure FX48mds_v2 is a compute-optimized, memory-intensive virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor providing 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores at a 4.2 GHz clock rate. The processor is configured with 2 threads per core, 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8), alongside hardware cryptographic extensions.

Hardware allocation is notable for combining high clock speed with an expansive memory footprint of 1008.0 GB RAM, delivering 21.0 GB per vCPU. Local ephemeral storage is bundled as a 2835 GB NVMe SSD, providing fast local I/O without requiring dedicated external storage attachments for transient data. The server does not include any GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show high single-core and multi-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2338.0 (top 10%) and a multi-core score of 20347.0 (top 25%). Stress-ng CPU tests recorded 2168.28 in single-core and 53295.74 in multi-core throughput. Memory subsystems demonstrated strong uncached performance, measuring 330.82 GB/sec read and 158.98 GB/sec write on 256 MB blocks, paired with 4138.71 GB/sec cached read throughput. Synthetic application workloads performed strongly, including 74.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 77.33 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

CPU-based LLM inference yields strong prompt processing metrics across diverse model sizes, including 2674.21 tokens/sec on a 135M model, 252.37 tokens/sec on a 7B model, and 33.02 tokens/sec on a 70B model. Text generation throughput scales moderately, recording 26.59 tokens/sec on a 7B model and 3.45 tokens/sec on a 70B model. For compute and memory density, the high core clock combined with 1008 GB RAM delivers strong performance per vCPU for single-threaded and in-memory operations.

Given the dense 1 TB memory array, high 4.2 GHz CPU frequency, and local NVMe storage, the FX48mds_v2 is suited for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), complex software builds, batch compression jobs, and intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure FX48mds_v2 is a compute-optimized, memory-intensive instance powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) and a 260 MB L3 cache. Featuring an x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and AMX instructions, it is equipped with 1008.0 GB of RAM and 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core performance (2338.0 Geekbench score) and strong memory throughput reaching 330.82 GB/sec uncached reads. The instance handled 74.99 million Redis SET operations per second and displayed robust throughput in CPU-driven LLM prompt processing. This configuration offers high density for memory-bound and frequency-sensitive enterprise tasks, making it suited for large-scale in-memory databases, EDA simulations, large code compilation pipelines, and transactional data processing.
